text:
ryan: hit a flake in our py-sdk where request IDs leak between concurrent async calls when using structlog + OTEL middleware. looks like headers are getting shared/mutated on the AsyncClient instance.
maria: can you share a tiny repro?
ryan: minimal: spawn two tasks that set a contextvar request_id then call the sdk's async client. sometimes logs show same id for both.
ryan: ```python
import asyncio
import contextvars
from redwood import AsyncClient  # wrapper around httpx in our sdk

request_id = contextvars.ContextVar('request_id')

async def worker(i):
    request_id.set(f"wid-{i}")
    async with AsyncClient() as c:
        await c.get('https://internal/api')

async def main():
    await asyncio.gather(worker(1), worker(2))

asyncio.run(main())
```
ryan: sometimes both requests end up logged with wid-1. repeating locally reproduces ~1/50 runs.
derek: that frequency screams shared mutable header map. in sync code we copy headers per-request, but IIRC for async we reused a dict to avoid allocations. bug.
jaen: small nit: our middleware typing is loose so it's easy to accidentally mutate fields. adding a TypedRequest/TypedHeaders Protocol would help.
maria: +1. also is the OTEL middleware reading request_id from contextvar or from span attributes? we try to attach both but that path might race.
derek: quick fix: make the middleware generate a fresh headers mapping per request and avoid in-place updates. longer-term: add typed hook signatures and an immutable Headers type. i'll take the bug fix PR.
jaen: I'll draft the typing PR and add an examples/observability/py sample that shows structlog + otel + async client working correctly under concurrency. test will assert request_id per-request.
ryan: thanks. one gotcha: when we schedule background tasks inside the SDK (we do that for streaming/cleanup), we need to capture contextvars at schedule time; otherwise created tasks may inherit a different context depending on caller. worth auditing places we call loop.create_task.
derek: good call. will grep for create_task usage and add a helper capture_context_and_create_task.
maria: perf note: copying headers per request has a cost; please add a tiny microbenchmark in the PR to show expected allocations. document tradeoff in the changelog.
derek: will add bench + perf test.
jaen: also proposing a small utility in redwood.sdk.observability: attach_request_id_from_context(ctx_var, logger, span) so apps don't have to wire structlog processors and otel attrs separately.
ci-bot: created issues #4187 (async-header-mutation) and #4188 (typed-middleware-hooks + observability-sample) and linked PR template.
ryan: perfect. assigning tasks in the issues. i'll add the repro artifacts and a failing unit test that reproduces the leak. :thumbsup:
